intro: The China business visa (M visa) is for commercial trips such as meetings, trade fairs, factory and supplier visits, and negotiating contracts. British passport holders can currently make short business trips visa-free, so you need an M visa if your stay is longer, you need multiple entries over a longer period, or you travel on another passport.

sections.heading: Do you need a China business visa?
sections.text: British passport holders can make business trips to China visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 December 2026. An M visa is still needed for longer stays, for multiple-entry visas covering regular trips, for travel after the visa-free policy ends if it isn't extended, and for UK residents travelling on other passports.

sections.heading: The invitation letter
sections.text: The most important document for an M visa is the invitation letter from the Chinese company or trade fair organiser. It should include your personal details, the purpose of the visit, the dates, where you'll go, who is paying, and the inviting company's details and signature. We check it against the visa centre's requirements before you apply.

sections.heading: Regular travel to China
sections.text: If you visit suppliers or partners in China often, a multiple-entry business visa can save repeated applications. We also arrange second British passports for frequent travellers who need one passport for travelling while the other is at a visa centre.

sections.heading: China business visa help in Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and help travellers and businesses across the North West and the rest of the UK. Most travel visa applications can be handled by post and email, so you don't need to visit us in person.

title: China Business Visa (M Visa) from the UK | Application Help
description: China business visa help for UK businesses: invitation letters, trade fairs, supplier visits, longer stays and visa-free rules for British citizens.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa for a short business trip?
faqs.a: If you travel on a British passport, short business trips are currently visa-free. We check the latest rules for your dates and passport before you book.

faqs.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
faqs.a: Often, yes, especially if you have visited China before. Tell us how often you travel and we will advise on the best visa to request.

faqs.q: Do I need to attend the visa centre?
faqs.a: Usually not. Until 31 December 2026, the Chinese Embassy in the UK has waived fingerprints for short-term visas (stays of up to 180 days), so we can submit your application and passport at the visa centre for you. Work visas and other long-stay visas still need fingerprints in person, and we book that appointment for you.

faqs.q: Can I attend the Canton Fair visa-free?
faqs.a: British passport holders can visit for business, including trade fairs, visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 December 2026. Other passport holders usually need an M visa.
